text: When fetuses die before day 35 (before bones form), the result is a small litter rather than mummification. Causes: Parvovirus (the main cause of small litters — selectively kills fetuses before day 35, which are fully reabsorbed with no bones, leaving litters of 3–6 piglets); endometritis (uterine damage after farrowing prevents the placenta developing normally over the whole uterine surface, leaving less implantation space for embryos — keeping the uterus clean matters: inject 2 ml oxytocin right after delivery to expel the whole placenta, then 1 ml Prostaglandin/Lutalyse 48 hours later to drain the uterus); poor semen quality (mating should last up to 15 minutes to deliver the full ~400 ml of semen — an interrupted mating, a boar serving twice a day, or a boar under 9 months old all reduce litter size); and movement/stress (sows should be moved either within 3 days of mating or not until at least 28 days after, since embryo implantation happens around day 13 — moving before implantation stresses the sow and reduces litter size).
